package_info.package_versions: N/A (modifies arbitrary native executables on infected systems)
package_info.why_malicious: Azov wiper is considered malicious because it injects destructive code into native Windows executables, causing them to irreversibly overwrite and corrupt user and system files with random data. The malware masquerades as ransomware but provides no means of recovery or decryption, making its primary intent data destruction rather than financial gain.

execution_context.trigger: When an infected native Windows executable (.exe, .dll) is launched by the user or system
execution_context.file_location: Injected into the code section of native Windows executables located throughout system drives (e.g., C:\Windows\System32\, user directories, and program folders)
required_permissions: permission to modify and execute native binaries
ability to enumerate files and directories

malicious_snippets.code_language: C/C++ (native Windows binary code, pseudocode shown)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When an infected executable is launched, the injected code enumerates files across system drives, overwrites file contents with random data, and corrupts file headers, resulting in irreversible destruction of user and system data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior is highly suspicious because legitimate executables do not inject code into other binaries or perform mass overwriting of unrelated files with random data upon execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Windows executables do not self-modify or inject destructive payloads into other binaries, nor do they irreversibly destroy user or system files without explicit user consent or a legitimate operational reason.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Secure file deletion utilities may overwrite files with random data, but only on user-selected targets and with explicit user authorization. System updates may modify executables, but only in controlled, signed, and verifiable ways.
key_indicators: Presence of injected code sections in native Windows executables
Mass file enumeration and overwriting with random or junk data
Corruption of file headers across multiple file types
Destructive actions triggered without user interaction or consent
No mechanism for data recovery or ransom payment

attack_chain.action: Initial infection: Azov wiper is delivered to the victim system, typically via phishing, trojanized software, or exploitation of vulnerabilities (exact vector may vary).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code injection into native executables

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into native Windows executables (.exe, .dll) located on the system, modifying their code sections to include the Azov wiper payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of destructive payload upon launch of infected executables

attack_chain.action: When an infected executable is launched, the injected Azov wiper code executes, enumerating files and overwriting their contents with random data, corrupting file headers, and causing irreversible data loss.
attack_chain.leads_to: Irreversible destruction of user and system data (final objective)

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected code injection or modification of native Windows executables (.exe, .dll) outside of legitimate update processes
Mass file enumeration and overwriting of file contents with random or junk data across multiple directories
Destructive file operations (overwriting, header corruption) initiated without user interaction or scheduled system tasks
Absence of any communication for ransom payment, decryption, or exfiltration
file_indicators: Native executables (.exe, .dll) with new or altered code sections not matching known legitimate versions
Files across system drives with contents replaced by random or non-recoverable data
Corrupted file headers in user and system files
No ransom notes or decryption instructions present on the system
network_indicators: No outbound network communication related to ransom payment, command and control, or data exfiltration
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to native Windows executables, such as the presence of new or altered code sections or mismatched hashes compared to trusted baselines. Detect mass file overwriting or corruption events, especially those occurring outside of legitimate update or deletion processes and without user initiation. Use endpoint protection to identify known Azov wiper signatures and behaviors. Alert on destructive file operations that do not match patterns of legitimate file shredding utilities or system updates. Correlate the absence of ransom notes or recovery instructions with observed destructive activity to distinguish from typical ransomware.
